title: Language as Trait, Politeness as Strategy: Controlled Tests of Linguistic Effects in LLM Social-Deduction Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.09768v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents coordinate through conversation, and the same message can be phrased in simpler or more complex language, bluntly or politely. We test whether such differences change how other agents judge and act, using the LURK Werewolf framework, which separates each utterance's speech-act predicate from its natural-language realization. We rewrite only the realization, check that the game content is preserved, and replay each game day from saved checkpoints against a re-sampled control. We vary linguistic range consistently across a speaker's messages and politeness strategy per utterance. Across 30 games and 4,335 replays, neither manipulation changes the trust other agents place in the speaker, and no effect on votes or night actions survives correction for multiple comparisons; the largest uncorrected effect is that shifting range away from a neutral paraphrase changes about 4 percentage points more of the other

translated_title: 语言作为特质，礼貌作为策略：LLM社交推理智能体中语言效应的受控测试
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体通过对话进行协调，同一条消息可以用更简单或更复杂的语言表达，也可以措辞得直率或礼貌。我们使用LURK狼人杀框架测试此类差异是否会改变其他智能体的判断和行动，该框架将每句话的言语行为谓词与其自然语言实现分离开来。我们仅重写实现部分，验证游戏内容得以保留，并从保存的检查点重放每个游戏日，与重新采样的对照组进行比较。我们在说话者的所有消息中一致地变化语言范围，并在每次发言中变化礼貌策略。在30场游戏和4,335次重放中，两种操纵均未改变其他智能体对说话者的信任，且对投票或夜间行动的影响在经过多重比较校正后均不显著；最大的未校正效应是，将语言范围从中性改述偏移会使其他
tldr: 该研究通过在狼人杀游戏中受控地改变LLM智能体语言复杂度与礼貌策略，发现这些语言风格差异对其他智能体的信任、投票和夜间行动均无显著影响。
en_tdlr: Controlled experiments in the LURK Werewolf framework show that varying the linguistic complexity and politeness of LLM agents' messages does not significantly affect other agents' trust, votes, or night actions.
